reasoning_content: The 401 error is occurring because the `startuphafen` client doesn't exist in the realm. The actual client IDs are `startuphafen_app` and `admin-cli`, so I need to use `startuphafen_app` as the client_id for the alice/marie password grant instead of the non-existent `startuphafen`.I need to use `startuphafen_app` as the client ID.

action.command: echo "=== alice via startuphafen_app ==="; curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:28080/realms/startuphafen/protocol/openid-connect/token -d "grant_type=password&client_id=startuphafen_app&username=alice&password=alice" -o /tmp/t_alice.json -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n"; python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('/tmp/t_alice.json')); t=d.get('access_token',''); import base64; p=t.split('.')[1]; p+='='*(-len(p)%4); print('alice roles:', json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(p)).get('realm_access',{}).get('roles'))" 2>/dev/null || head -c 200 /tmp/t_alice.json; echo; echo "=== marie via startuphafen_app ==="; curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:28080/realms/startuphafen/protocol/openid-connect/token -d "grant_type=password&client_id=startuphafen_app&username=marie&password=marie" -o /tmp/t_marie.json -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n"; python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('/tmp/t_marie.json')); t=d.get('access_token',''); import base64; p=t.split('.')[1]; p+='='*(-len(p)%4); print('marie roles:', json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(p)).get('realm_access',{}).get('roles'))" 2>/dev/null || head -c 200 /tmp/t_marie.json
